summary: Balances and transaction history now persist in one validated versioned snapshot with atomic replacement, count footer, failure cleanup and explicit legacy migration.
Service-owned account copies prevent callers from changing balances outside commands; detached snapshots capture both collections under one synchronized service boundary.
Money precision, account balances, transaction relationships, duplicate identities and missing references are validated on entry and load.
Transfers construct their history before mutation; competing withdrawals cannot overdraw one shared service instance.
Holder rename and confirmed deletion of only unused zero-balance accounts teach domain-aware CRUD while preserving used-account history.
Nine detailed course documents and a Java 17 runner explain actual source, ownership, consistency, migration, tests, traces and progressive database/HTTP/idempotency exercises.

checks.environment: Microsoft OpenJDK 17.0.10; --release 17 -Xlint:all; real temporary files; eight-thread withdrawal competition; isolated source

limits: Local simulator only; no HTTP, browser, database, authentication or external financial service.
Synchronization is per service instance; no cross-process stale-save protection or power-loss guarantee.
Commands mutate memory before saving; save failure exits CLI without success but the service has no persistence rollback unit of work.
Snapshot validates fields, references and counts but does not reconcile historical balances or cryptographically verify integrity; no shared transfer ID.
Legacy files remain unchanged and become stale after migration; old binaries must not be alternated against the same data.
Atomic replacement is required; CLI failures are text diagnostics without a structured failure exit-code contract.
